why:
Summed panel scores across all five criteria and three judges: case-study 125 (ECD 42, prospect 41, producer 42), parallel-journey 113 (38 / 40 / 35), canvas 97 (33 / 31 / 33). Case-study has the best total, and it also leads explains_what_was_built (27 against 22 and 21) and feasibility. It loses premium_and_real to parallel-journey, so this plan keeps case-study's skeleton: numbered chapters, short independent takes, the 112.5 BPM grid, the phone-to-desktop finder handoff and full coverage of the build. It then fixes every fatal flaw the judges named.

1. Too much text. There are now seven short statements, each one or two lines and 11 words or fewer, plus one event-synced line. There are no support lines, the labels are short ('01 — HOME'), and there are two motion chips instead of three ms annotations. Every statement stays readable for at least 1.9 s.
2. Cormorant beside The Seasons. Orbit's voice is now General Sans and Cabinet Grotesk only, both already in app/fonts. The client's serif appears only inside the real pages.
3. Keynote grammar (locked camera, devices sliding in on cue, five cuts). The devices are now fixed objects on one Linen table and only the camera moves: a pull-back, two trucks and a final pull-back, all eased, with lean of 2° or less and screen speed of 1,500 px/s or less. There are 3 hard cuts instead of 5. Each one lands on a bar downbeat and is a change of camera setup motivated by on-screen action: a match cut on the product, a chapter cut, and the finder handoff.
4. The −7° tabletop arc is gone. The finale is a flat pull-back.
5. Different products in the bag (prospect). The phone and the desktop both buy Raw Seduction, EGP 970, and both meters were verified live: 'EGP 1,230 away', then 'EGP 980 away' after the mystery box, then 'EGP 260 away' after +1.
6. The producer's build issues. Motion blur now follows one rule: 120 Hz takes averaged 1:2:1 over a 180° shutter. The IntersectionObserver is flushed every frame with real rAFs. The cursor is driven with page.mouse along the logged path, and paths run through card and chip gutters so only the intended elements hover. Image routing is set per take, against verified local files. There is no edge bleed: every device is fully in frame or fully out.

From parallel-journey: the continuous camera on a lit stage, desktop and phone acting in call and response, the URL pill showing the path only, the studio voice in General Sans, the large 'Orbit' signature on the final chord, the honest credit line and click pans that follow the device. Its double finder is replaced by case-study's handoff. From canvas: the line synced to an on-screen event, the inspect-style chip, the cursor sprite read from the computed CSS cursor, and the URL pill updating live. Both of canvas's flaws are avoided: the 'Acqua di Giò' name never appears (Raw Seduction has no inspired-by line), and every click really navigates.

Every coordinate and string used in this plan was checked against the running production build on localhost:3000 on 2026-10-09.

title: eternal — a storefront by Orbit (case study, 30 s, desktop and phone)
logline: One storefront runs live on two screens set on a Linen table. The site opens itself with its own loader. The phone holds the Instagram-ad first screen while the desktop browses into the eterno catalogue. Both land on Raw Seduction and add it to the same bag, a sheet on the phone and a drawer on desktop. The scent finder starts on the phone and finishes on desktop from the link. The camera then pulls back to 'Designed and built by Orbit.' Short numbered statements explain each part, on an original 112.5 BPM track the picture is cut to.
rules: Every pixel inside a device is the production build (next start on localhost:3000) captured frame-exactly on a virtual clock. The film draws nothing inside the screens except the cursor and touch marks.
No CG objects, no void, no bloom, particles, light shafts, chromatic aberration, vignette, glow wipes, fly-throughs or LUT. Site pixels are composited 1:1 in sRGB with no grade.
Devices are fixed physical objects on one Linen table and never slide, fade or scale on their own. Only the camera moves, and only between the five framings defined in visual_system.
Exactly 3 hard cuts (12.800, 21.333, 23.467), each on a bar downbeat and each a change of camera setup motivated by on-screen action. There are no dissolves.

Every change of picture inside a screen is the site's own behaviour, triggered by a visible click or tap or by a scroll: the loader curtain, PageFade, header switch, line hover, FLIP re-flow, card hover, sticky bar, sheet, drawer, meters, finder slide, composing mark and the results swap.

A device may change page off-frame only if that change is never shown: the desktop during bars 7–8 and 11, the phone during bars 5–6 and 12. Every join between takes is hidden off-frame or verified pixel-identical (D1→D2 at 9.000).

Overlays sit only on clean Linen, never over a page or a device. Each enters on a beat with the site's rise (16 px, 600 ms, ease-emphasized) and has fully left 0 ms or more before the camera move or cut that would cross it.

Overlay copy comes only from the verified claims list: no metrics, no '43', no reviews, no launch or live-domain claim, no third-party fragrance names, no timelines, and no credit for the client's identity or photography.
Faces: General Sans Regular and Cabinet Grotesk Regular from app/fonts only. Never The Seasons (demo licence, missing glyphs) and never Cormorant.

Capture hygiene in every take: fresh context, consent cookie, eternal.loaded set (except D1), never an Instagram/FBAN/FBAV UA or utm/fbclid/gclid, reducedMotion 'no-preference', .wa-float hidden, carets transparent, scroll-behavior auto, Shopify images routed to the product's own local photos.

Scrolls run on the live viewport: an eased scrollTo with behavior 'instant' per 120 Hz step. They are never wheel scrolls and never full-page strips, because the header switch, parallax, sticky bar and reveals are scroll-driven.

The pointer moves only along logged paths through gutters (the column gutter x 382–406, the gap between the chip row and the first card row, the right gutter x 1360–1440), so only the intended elements hover. Phones are driven with page.tap only.
The beat grid is 112.5 BPM: beat = 16 frames, bar = 64 frames. Clicks and taps land on beats or half-beats, and site timers (450, 280 and 600 ms) fall where they really fall.
Both devices are large whenever they are in frame: desktop at 0.79–0.81 css scale in SPLIT and DESK, phone at 0.94 in SPLIT and 1.07–1.09 in PHONE. WIDE (0.66) is used only under the end card.
Motion blur is a 180° shutter: each output frame averages the sub-frames at t−8.333, t and t+8.333 ms, weighted 1:2:1, for camera motion and site motion alike.
visual_system:
FRAME: 1920×1080, 30 fps, 900 frames. Master H.264 High 4:2:0, tagged BT.709 for primaries, transfer and matrix, limited range.

STAGE: one infinite Linen #F3EFE7 table. Stage units equal output px at camera k=1.
- Light: a broad, soft Paper #FAF8F3 radial falloff from the upper left, fixed to the stage, at most +2% luminance at the hot spot. Camera moves therefore reveal a real surface, not a flat fill.
- Grain: monochrome dither at σ ≈ 1.2/255, re-seeded per frame, over the whole frame. It is only there to stop banding.
- Forbidden: vignette, bloom, particles, light shafts, chromatic aberration and any colour grade.

FIXED LAYOUT on the table (stage px):
- Browser window: x 120–1254, y 281–1030. The chrome bar is y 281–321 (40 px). The viewport is y 321–1030, 1440×900 css at 0.7875.
- Phone body: x 1407–1800, y 166–1030, 418×919 css at 0.94. Screen inset 13, status bar 44, viewport 367×793.
- Gap between the devices: 153 px.
- The phone sits at z +18 px, so it shows a little real parallax when the camera leans.

FRAMINGS. The camera is a centre (cx, cy) in stage px, a zoom k, and a lean in rotateY with 2400 px perspective. A solver keeps on-screen boxes within ±1 px of the positions below.
- OPEN: k 2.20, centre (687,675). The frame lies wholly inside the desktop viewport and the loader mark draws at about 222 px.
- SPLIT: k 1.00, centre (960,540). Desktop on screen at x 120–1254, y 281–1030. Phone at x 1407–1800, y 166–1030. Text band at y 72–255, x 120–1254.
- DESK: k 1.00, centre (390,655). Desktop at x 690–1824, y 166–915. Phone fully off frame to the right. Text column at x 120–610.
- PHONE: k 1.14, centre (2132,598). Phone at x 134–582, y 48–1032, about 1.07 css scale. Desktop fully off frame to the left (its right edge at −41). Text column at x 700–1720.
- WIDE: k 0.66, centre (514,568). Both devices at x 700–1809, y 275–845. Credit column at x 120–620.

CAMERA RULES:
- Moves use log-scale zoom with the centre path coupled to the zoom.
- Trucks ease in and out on a sine curve. Screen speed peaks at about 840 px/s (SPLIT→DESK) and about 1,230 px/s (PHONE→SPLIT), always 1,500 px/s or less.
- Lean is up to 2° into the direction of travel, only while moving, and back to 0 at rest.
- Holds drift no more than 1.5% scale and 12 px per bar, so no frame is frozen.
- Velocity is continuous everywhere except at the three cuts. tools/path.mjs verifies this.

MOTION BLUR AND SHARPNESS:
- Site takes are recorded at 120 Hz. Each output frame renders 3 sub-frames, at t−8.333, t and t+8.333 ms, with matching take frames and camera poses, averaged 1:2:1 (a 180° shutter).
- Desktop takes are captured at DPR 2. They show at no more than 1.73 px per css px (OPEN), so they are always supersampled.
- Phone takes are captured at DPR 3 and show at no more than 1.09 px per css px.
- Takes are pre-scaled with Lanczos3 into two mip levels: full size for OPEN, and 1440 px wide for everything else.

INPUT MARKS (the only things drawn over UI):
- Desktop cursor: an arrow or a hand, chosen per frame from the logged computed cursor. Night fill with a 1.5 px Linen outline and a 2 px soft shadow, drawn at 24 css px. It moves exactly along the page.mouse path and scales to 0.92 for the press (mouse down to mouse up). It rests in the right gutter while not in use.
- Phone touch mark: a 44 css px disc, Night at 14% fill with a 1.5 px Night 25% ring. It appears 2 frames before the tap, scaling from 0.85 to 1 over 120 ms, fades over 240 ms, and sits on the logged tap point.

COLOUR: the encode is checked after decoding. A Linen patch and a Night UI patch must both be within ΔE<2.

PHONE, generic: no notch or island, no logo, no side buttons, no home indicator.

- Body: 418 × 919 css units, which is 393 × 864 stage px at 0.94. Night #171614, outer radius 58 css.
- Rim: a 1.5 px highlight just inside the edge, a gradient from rgba(255,255,255,.18) at the top to .04 at the bottom.
- Screen: inset 14 css, 390 × 891 css (a 47 css status bar plus the 844 css viewport), screen radius 44 css.
- Punch-hole camera: a 10 css px circle in #0B0A09 with a 1 px rgba(255,255,255,.06) ring, centred horizontally, 18 css below the screen top.
- Status bar, drawn by us:
  - Its fill is sampled per frame from the page's top pixel row (the centre 60%, averaged). That is Night under the announcement bar and dimmed Night under the bag backdrop.
  - Glyphs: the time '10:08' in General Sans 15 css, plus signal, wifi and battery as simple vectors. They are Linen #F3EFE7 when the sampled luminance is below 0.5, otherwise Night.

SHADOWS: one key light, overhead and slightly from the left, so every layer is offset +4 px in x. Values are in stage px and scale with k. Each shadow travels with its object, and under lean it is projected on the table plane.
- Browser: 0 1 2 rgba(23,22,20,.10); 0 10 24 rgba(23,22,20,.07); 0 34 70 −14 rgba(23,22,20,.16).
- Phone (closer to the lens): 0 2 3 rgba(23,22,20,.14); 0 14 28 rgba(23,22,20,.10); 0 44 80 −16 rgba(23,22,20,.20).
- The devices never overlap, so neither casts onto the other.

SCREENS: emissive and exact. There is no glare, reflection, tint or grade on any captured pixel.
type_system:
VOICE: Orbit speaks in grotesks. The client's serif, The Seasons, appears only inside the real captured pages. Overlays never use The Seasons (an evaluation-only demo that lacks 4, the hyphen, the apostrophe and the ampersand) or Cormorant.

FACES, Regular cuts only and never synthesized bold:
- General Sans Regular (app/fonts/general-sans/GeneralSans-Regular.woff2) for statements, the synced line, the end card and the signature.
- Cabinet Grotesk Regular (app/fonts/cabinet-grotesk/CabinetGrotesk-Regular.woff2) for labels, chips and the stack line, always in capitals.
- Glyphs to check before building: the em dash —, the middle dot ·, the curly apostrophe ’ and the ellipsis.

COLOURS: Night #171614 for statements; Ash #5F584F for labels and secondary lines; the gold text colour #8F5B1B for chapter numbers ('01'–'05'); Golden hour #B97A2B for the synced line's 6 px dot; Dune #CDBFA5 for the hairlines.

STYLES at 1080p:
- STATEMENT: General Sans 56 px on a 62 px line, tracking −0.015em, Night, left-aligned with manual breaks. In the band, at most 2 lines on a 1,130 px measure. In columns, at most 3 lines of 17 characters or fewer. Each line's width is measured at build time; if one does not fit, the size drops to 52 px, never lower, and the breaks never change.
- LABEL: Cabinet Grotesk 20 px capitals, tracking +0.16em, Ash, with the chapter number in #8F5B1B. Its cap-top sits 30 px above the statement's cap height.
- SYNCED LINE (one use only): General Sans 30 px on a 40 px line, Night, preceded by a 6 px Golden hour dot. It appears on the exact frame of the event it names.
- CHIP (two uses only): Cabinet Grotesk 18 px capitals, tracking +0.14em, Night on a Paper #FAF8F3 pill with square corners (like the site's buttons), a 1 px Dune hairline and 8/12 padding. It sits in the nearest clean Linen, aligned to the UI element it names.
- END CARD:
  - Label: Cabinet Grotesk 20 px capitals, Ash.
  - 'Designed and built by': General Sans 40/48, Night.
  - Signature 'Orbit': General Sans 144 px, tracking −0.03em, Night. If Orbit's own SVG logo is supplied it replaces this at the same cap height; nothing is invented.
  - Hairline: Dune 1 px, 480 px wide.
  - Services: General Sans 24/34, Ash.
  - Stack: Cabinet Grotesk 18 px capitals, Ash.
  - Fine print: General Sans 16 px, Ash.

POSITIONS:
- BAND (SPLIT): x 120; label cap-top at y 84; statement baselines at y 160 and 222. Chip C2 is right-aligned at x 1254 on the label line.
- LEFT COLUMN (DESK): x 120–610; block centred on y 540. Chip C1 sits under the desktop at y 942–974, its left edge at x 900, level with the Woody chip.
- RIGHT COLUMN (PHONE): x 700–1720; label cap-top at y 300; statement baselines at y 390 and 452; synced line baseline at y 532.
- END (WIDE): x 120–620. Label cap-top at y 330; 'Designed and built by' baseline at y 410; 'Orbit' baseline at y 548; hairline at y 600; services baselines at y 650 and 684; stack at y 730; fine print at y 790. The block centres on y 560, level with the devices.

ANIMATION, the site's own tokens:
- In: each line rises 16 px while fading in, over 600 ms on ease-emphasized, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1). Lines stagger by 80 ms in the order label, statement lines, synced or detail line. Chips rise 4 px and fade over 200 ms on ease-standard, cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). The signature rises 24 px over 600 ms on ease-emphasized.
- Out: fade plus 8 px upward over 200 ms on ease-standard. The exit always ends at or before the cut or camera move that would cross its zone.
- No per-letter effects, masks, blur-ins or tracking animation.

READABILITY:
- A 56 px statement plays at about 11–12 px on a portrait phone and about 25 px in landscape, so every statement must stand on its own.
- Every statement is held for at least 1.9 s after its rise. Most are held 2.4–3.2 s.
- Total overlay copy is about 80 words, around 20% less than the case-study draft. It has no support lines and no ms annotations beyond the two chips.
transition_grammar:
1) CAMERA, NOT SLIDES. The devices are props fixed on one table, and the only things that move them on screen are camera moves between five framings. There are four camera moves, each motivated by something on screen:
- The pull-back out of the loader (0.8–2.133), motivated by the curtain lifting.
- The truck from SPLIT to DESK (8.533–9.600), following the desktop's click into the catalogue.
- The pull-back from PHONE to SPLIT (17.067–18.667), motivated by the sheet opening and leading to the same bag on desktop.
- The final pull-back from DESK to WIDE (25.600–27.400), as the matches land and the work is shown whole.
Moves start on bar downbeats. Trucks use a sine ease-in-out and pull-backs land with zero velocity. Lean is 2° or less, only while moving, and screen speed is 1,500 px/s or less. Between moves the camera drifts by 1.5% or less per bar and is never frozen.

2) THREE HARD CUTS, all on bar downbeats and all changes of camera setup (coverage, not slides):
- 12.800 (bar 7), DESK to PHONE: a match cut on the product. The desktop clicks Raw Seduction and the page fades; we cut to the phone, already on Raw Seduction from its hero tap at 8.267.
- 21.333 (bar 11), SPLIT to PHONE: the chapter cut into the finder, on the swell where the kick drops out.
- 23.467 (bar 12), PHONE to DESK: the handoff. The URL pill shows the phone's answers carried in the link.
There are no other cuts and no dissolves, wipes, glows or fly-throughs.

3) THE SITE'S OWN TRANSITIONS change everything inside the screens: the G1 loader curtain, G2 PageFade at 200 ms, the header switch, the line-still crossfade, the FLIP re-flow, the card hover, the sticky bar (240 ms), the bag sheet and the drawer (320 ms ease-emphasized), the meters (600 ms), the finder screen slide (320 ms), the composing mark and the finder's own hard swap to results. Each is triggered by a visible click, tap or scroll, captured on the virtual clock and never retimed.

4) CALL AND RESPONSE. When both screens are in frame, one acts and the other answers half a beat or one beat later (8.000 desktop, then 8.267 phone; 19.733 phone, then 20.267 desktop). Two inputs never land in the same beat.

5) TYPE follows the camera. Text enters on a beat once its zone is clear and has fully left before any move or cut crosses that zone. Chips appear on the first frame of the animation they name.

6) SOUND marks only real events: clicks and taps panned to the device's on-screen position, two air brushes under the sheet and the drawer, swells into the downbeats of bars 3, 7, 11, 13 and 14, a felt note on the bar-12 cut, and the final chord under 'Orbit'. Camera moves get no whooshes.

build_steps: 1. Lock the edit as data. Write reel/showcase/v2/edit.json with: the grid (112.5 BPM, 16 frames per beat, 64 per bar); the seven takes with their film↔take offsets, warm-ups and holds; every input event; the camera keys and the three cuts; every overlay with its in and out times; and the audio cue. The recorder, the compositor and score.py all read this one file. Keep the v1 files.

2. Extend tools/record.mjs.
- Per-take fps of 120; waitUntil 'domcontentloaded' ('commit' for D1) followed by settle(); a pre-warm pass.
- CDP Animation.enable and setPlaybackRate(0) after settle; an IntersectionObserver flush of two real rAFs after each vc.advance.
- New actions: 'glide' (page.mouse along a cubic path with an ease, logged per frame), 'press' (mouse down and up at the current point), 'tap' (page.tap at a measured centre, logged), and scroll with a custom curve.
- A per-take image route map (packshot → -2 or -3) and eager decoding of every img.
- 'warm' and 't0' options; 'resetOnStart' for D1 and P1.
- A per-frame meta log: pointer x/y, computed cursor, pressed state, url path+search, hovered element selector, and the top-row colour on phones.

3. Add the seven v2 takes to tools/takes.mjs (v2-d1-open-home, v2-d2-shop, v2-d3-pdp-bag, v2-d4-finder, v2-p1-home, v2-p2-pdp-bag, v2-p3-finder) with timelines in film seconds, exactly as listed in captures.

4. Probe pass (record.mjs --probe: DPR 1, 30 Hz, no image writes).
- Confirm every coordinate in this plan: the eterno row, the Woody chip, raw-seduction at doc (406,1755) after the filter, Add (1077,409), + (1191,225), the hero link (166,455), the sticky bar (283,812), the box Add (326,599), Her (105,308), Night (195,363), Arm’s length (720,541).
- Tune P2's scroll curve so .pdp-bar mounts on frame 448.
- Check from the hover log that the pointer paths only hover the intended elements.
- Check for no 'INSPIRED BY', no '[' brackets, no data-ad, no broken images, no WhatsApp float and no consent banner.

5. Record the takes: RECORD_JOBS=3, about 4,760 frames, roughly 1 h at the measured 1.7–2.1 s per frame per job, about 5 GB of the 27 GB free. Then make a contact sheet per take, run the D1→D2 join diff at film 9.000, and spot-check stills at every event frame.

6. Score. Edit reel/showcase/music/score.py:
- BPM = 112.5 (BEAT 0.5333, BAR 2.1333). 14 bars end at 29.867; LENGTH stays 30.0.
- Clicks and whooshes become [time, pan, gain] triples.
- Add accents: the C6 bell at 0.600, the air rise 0.45–1.00, the felt C5 at 23.467, bell 16ths 24.280–24.880, and the dyad at 24.880.
- Keep the sections keys_pads 1–2, groove_a 3–6, groove_b 7–10, lift 11–12, full 13, end 14, and the swells at bars 3, 7, 11, 13 and 14.
Write music/cue-v2.json from edit.json and render. Master in two loudnorm passes to −14 LUFS and −1 dBTP. Run analyze.py to check that the click onsets fall within ±1 frame of the film events and the downbeats on frames 64·n.

8. Pre-render checks.
- tools/path.mjs: screen speed 1,500 px/s or less, lean 2° or less, no velocity jumps except at frames 384, 640 and 704, drift 1.5% or less per bar.
- A per-frame overlap test: no overlay box intersects a device box or its shadow.
- A text-measure test: every line fits its column at 56 px, falling back to 52.
- A glyph test for —, ·, ’ and ….
- The determinism check: preview --check at 9.0, 19.8 and 24.9.

9. Draft render: 1 sub-frame at 960×540 for the timing review, then contact sheets at every event frame. Fix, then render the master with 3 sub-frames in chunks 0–10, 10–20 and 20–30, joined with concat -c copy. Fix individual moments later with tools/splice.mjs.

10. Encode and deliver.
- Master: ffmpeg H.264 High, yuv420p, scale out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv, -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709, CRF 14 capped at 20 Mb/s, AAC 320 kb/s 48 kHz, +faststart → out/v2/eternal-orbit-case-study.mp4.
- Web version at 6 Mb/s.
- A web-loop variant: identical, but fading to bare Linen over 29.6–30.0.
- Poster JPEGs: frame 885 (the end card) and frame 594 (19.8 s, drawer and sheet side by side).
- Decode the master and check Linen #F3EFE7 and Night #171614 patches are within ΔE<2.
11. Panel review against the checklist, then splice fixes. Update reel/showcase/README.md (the v2 sequence, takes and rebuild commands) and mark tasks #6–#9 done.
review_checklist: BRIEF, desktop and mobile: both devices are large whenever in frame, and the pair shares the frame for about 17 s (0–8.5, 17.1–21.3, 25.6–30). Each device has about 6.4 s solo. No bottle-only or CG shot exists.

BRIEF, explanation: each of the six chapters (home, catalogue/headless, product page, bag, finder, credit) has one numbered statement. A cold viewer watching once can say what Orbit built, on what stack, and for which traffic. Test with 3 people at laptop size and at phone size.

BRIEF, music: it is original (score.py and numpy only). The downbeats fall on frames 64·n. The three cuts sit on swells or the felt note. The lift runs into the full bar and the final chord carries 'Orbit'. The film ends in silence at 30.000.

TRUTH: every overlay line matches its evidence. Nowhere in the overlays: '43', metrics, reviews, 'Bestseller', launch or live-domain claims, timelines or third-party fragrance names. Scan every frame's OCR for 'INSPIRED BY' and '['; both must be absent. The URL pill shows the path only.

CREDIT HYGIENE: the end card credits Orbit for direction, wireframes, design system, motion, front-end and Shopify integration only. 'Brand marks and photography: eternal.' is present. No Orbit mark is invented; Orbit's SVG is used if it has been supplied, otherwise the typeset signature.

REAL, NOT FAKE: every change inside a screen is the site's own behaviour, traced to a logged click, tap or scroll. There are no film-made wipes, dissolves, glows or fly-throughs. There are exactly 3 cuts, at frames 384, 640 and 704, and the devices never move except by camera.

TIMING, at 30 fps output frames: eterno click 240, phone hero tap 248, Woody 320, card click 376, sticky bar mounts 448 (±1), sticky tap 464, sheet 477–478, desktop Add 560, drawer 573–574, box Add 592, +1 608, Her 656, Night 688, Arm’s length 720, results swap 746, 'Orbit' 832.

SAME PRODUCT: Raw Seduction at EGP 970 on both screens. Meters read 'EGP 1,230 away', then 'EGP 980 away' on the phone and 'EGP 260 away' on desktop. Gallery frame 1 is the apples still, and no duplicate frame is ever visible.

CAPTURE HYGIENE: html[data-ad] absent in every take; no WhatsApp float, consent banner, input carets or scrollbars; no broken images (naturalWidth>0 for every in-view img); lazy images never pop in; the D1→D2 join diff is below 0.5/255; the hover log shows only the intended targets (the eterno line, the Woody chip, the raw-seduction card, Add, +, Arm’s length).

CAMERA: screen speed 1,500 px/s or less; lean 2° or less and zero at rest; C1-continuous except at the 3 cuts; drift 1.5% or less per bar; no frame fully frozen except the end card's 0.5% breathing hold; no device bleeds partly off the frame edge at rest.

TYPE: General Sans and Cabinet Grotesk only, never The Seasons or Cormorant, never faux bold. Lines fit their measure at 56 px (52 at minimum). No overlay touches a device or shadow. Every exit completes before its cut or move. Statements are readable for at least 1.9 s. —, ·, ’ and … render in the woff2 files.

LOOK: Linen stage with a Paper falloff of 2% or less; no vignette, bloom, particles, chromatic aberration or grade; dither invisible at 100%. Device frames are generic: no notch, no traffic lights, no Apple hardware cues. Shadows travel with their objects.
COLOUR: the master is tagged BT.709 for primaries, transfer and matrix. Linen #F3EFE7 and Night #171614 patches are within ΔE<2 after decoding, and the campaign photography is not tinted.

AUDIO: −14 LUFS ±0.5 integrated; true peak −1 dBTP or lower; ticks about −30 dBFS and air brushes −32 dBFS or quieter; pans follow each device's on-screen position (desktop clicks negative in SPLIT and positive in DESK; phone taps positive in SPLIT and negative in PHONE); no whoosh on camera moves; no clipping.

MOTION BLUR: the 3-tap 1:2:1 180° shutter is applied to camera and site motion alike. The fast desktop scroll (11.2–12.0) and the trucks do not strobe at 30 fps; if they do, slow the move rather than adding blur.

DECISIONS FOR THE USER before public release: (a) The Seasons is an evaluation-only demo font and it renders inside every capture of the site, so the client should license it or accept the risk. (b) Supply the Orbit SVG logo and any studio URL. (c) Confirm General Sans and Cabinet Grotesk (Fontshare) licences cover use in video. (d) Confirm the client is happy for the eternal site to appear before its launch on its own domain; the film shows no domain.

DELIVERABLES: the master mp4 with music, the web mp4, the web-loop variant, and both posters. The README is updated with the v2 sequence and rebuild commands. Consider a 4:5 recut later for Instagram and Behance mobile, by re-keying the camera on the same takes.
